text: SLAs and SLOs — three related terms, and how they actually fit together.
An SLI is the actual measured number. An SLO is the internal target a team holds itself to. An SLA is the external promise, like lesson 50's data contract. Same underlying thing, different audiences.
An error budget turns an SLO into something spendable — the small allowed slack you can use on deploys or experiments, rather than an abstract number nobody acts on.
Setting the SLO equal to the SLA leaves no room for anything to go even slightly wrong. Setting it stricter builds in a buffer — normal noise eats into that margin first.
A disciplined way of using metrics and alerts already built. Next up: incident response — what actually happens when the SLO gets breached.
